data.name: Monitor_VoltageImplausible
data.value: ⚠ Measured voltage ({0} V) doesn't match the selected supply voltage — check the 24V/56V setting.

data.name: Monitor_AngleGuardTripped
data.value: 🔴 Motor disarmed by safety check: current was flowing with no torque requested and the wheel still — meaning it was turning into heat, not force. Usually the calibration finished but stored a wrong electrical angle (motor phases reconnected in a different order, encoder remounted). Power-cycle the base to run a fresh calibration. It will NOT re-arm on its own.

data.name: Update_Warning
data.value: Do not disconnect the device while updating — interrupting the flash can leave it unusable.

data.name: Save_ToController_Tip
data.value: Stores the steering angle and centre in the base's flash. Force drops for about a second while it writes.

data.name: Center_Hotkey_Empty
data.value: No shortcut — click Assign and press a button or key.

data.name: Center_Hotkey_Capturing
data.value: Hold the button/combo (or the keys, e.g. Ctrl + F9) and release to confirm…

data.name: SettingHelp_MotionRange
data.value: How many degrees the wheel turns lock to lock. E.g. 900 degrees is the road-car standard; formula and GT cars usually run 360 to 540.

data.name: SettingHelp_SoftStopRange
data.value: How many degrees BEFORE the end of travel the end-stop wall starts acting. Higher = more progressive. E.g. 8 degrees ramps the force up instead of hitting a hard wall.

data.name: SettingHelp_SoftStopStrength
data.value: Stiffness of the wall at the end of travel. E.g. 70% gives a firm wall; 100% returns a lot of energy and can catapult the wheel if damping is low.

data.name: SettingHelp_TotalStrength
data.value: Overall FFB strength: scales everything the game sends. E.g. 100% uses the configured peak torque; 60% makes the wheel lighter without touching anything else.

data.name: SettingHelp_SpringStrength
data.value: Spring pulling the wheel back to center even when the game does not ask. E.g. helps in games with weak self-aligning torque; 0% leaves the wheel loose.

data.name: SettingHelp_DamperStrength
data.value: Wheel heaviness: resists how fast you turn. E.g. raise it if the wheel feels nervous or oscillates on its own.

data.name: SettingHelp_StaticDamping
data.value: Constant friction, present even when the wheel is still. E.g. 5% removes the loose feeling on straights without making steering heavy.

data.name: SettingHelp_MaxTorqueLimit
data.value: Torque ceiling as a percentage of the base maximum. E.g. 50% caps peak force to protect the motor or to suit a beginner.

data.name: SettingHelp_ForceDirection
data.value: Flips the direction of the force. E.g. use it if the wheel pulls the wrong way through a corner.

data.name: SettingHelp_EndstopDamping
data.value: Brake for the end-stop wall: absorbs the impact energy instead of returning it. E.g. 0% makes the wheel bounce and shoot back; 35% makes it settle against the stop.

data.name: SettingHelp_Linearity
data.value: Force response curve. 100% = linear; below emphasises weak forces, above emphasises strong ones. E.g. 80% brings out more road detail at low force.

data.name: SettingHelp_SlewRate
data.value: Smooths abrupt force changes between cycles. E.g. raise it if you feel hard jolts over kerbs.

data.name: SettingHelp_ReconstructionSteps
data.value: Steps used to reconstruct force between game packets. E.g. higher values smooth games that send at 60 Hz.

data.name: SettingHelp_ReconstructionLpf
data.value: Extra filter applied to the reconstructed force. E.g. raise it if high-frequency hiss remains.

data.name: SettingHelp_BoardVariant
data.value: Board variant: 24 V or 56 V. Sets the bus voltage reading scale. E.g. with a 27 V supply the board is the 56 V one. Getting this wrong makes the base read the wrong voltage.

data.name: SettingHelp_BusNominalV
data.value: Voltage of the supply feeding the base. E.g. 27 V. Used to derive overvoltage limits and brake resistor behaviour.

data.name: SettingHelp_PositionSmoothing
data.value: Smoothing applied to the encoder position before the force calculation. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_PowerLimit
data.value: Power limit delivered to the motor, as a percentage. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_BrakingLimit
data.value: Limit for the current fed back to the supply when the wheel is braked. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_OutputFilterHz
data.value: Smooths the force that comes out by cutting frequencies above this value. Use it only if the wheel shakes once everything else is dialled in. E.g. 0 is off (default); start at 100 Hz and come down slowly until the shake goes. CAREFUL: over-filtering is the most common cause of FFB with no detail — every Hz you remove erases road texture along with the shake.

data.name: SettingHelp_OscGuardEnable
data.value: Damps the wheel ONLY when it enters self-oscillation — the shake that shows up after you raise the low end of the force curve and the wheel-driver-base loop starts feeding itself. Unlike Damper, which is always on and eats road texture all the time, this guard stays out of the way while you feel the track and only steps in during the episode. It recognises oscillation by its rhythm (direction reversals at short, regular intervals), which normal steering and kerbs do not have. E.g. turn it on if the base shakes on the straight after you boosted small forces in the curve.

data.name: SettingHelp_CoggingEnable
data.value: Use the cogging compensation table stored in flash. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_EncoderDirection
data.value: Flips the direction the base REPORTS — use it if the wheel turns one way and the screen (or the game) shows the other, which happens when the sensor is mounted mirrored. E.g. -1 to flip, 1 to leave as is. It does NOT touch the motor's internal direction: calibration works that out on its own. Only takes effect after the base reboots.

data.name: SettingHelp_EncoderCpr
data.value: Encoder resolution. On ABZ, enter the PULSES PER REVOLUTION printed on the label — the app applies the x4 quadrature. E.g. a 1000 P/R E6B2 becomes 4000 counts.

data.name: SettingHelp_EncoderType
data.value: Sensor MODEL you bought. E.g. E6B2-CWZ6C (incremental) or MT6701 (magnetic). The technology list below changes with the model.

data.name: SettingHelp_EncoderInterface
data.value: Wiring TECHNOLOGY: only the options the chosen model offers are shown. E.g. the E6B2 is ABZ; the MT6701 accepts ABZ or SSI.

data.name: SettingHelp_PolePairs
data.value: Motor pole pairs (magnet count divided by 2). E.g. 15 on the hoverboard motor. Getting this wrong drives current into the wrong coil: heat without torque.

data.name: SettingHelp_CalibrationCurrent
data.value: Current used to calibrate the encoder at boot. E.g. 5 A overcomes the hoverboard motor cogging. It is automatically capped at the motor current limit.

data.name: SettingHelp_SoftPowerEnable
data.value: Enables software shutdown of the DC bus. Requires the hardware to be wired. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_PowerButtonEnable
data.value: Enables the physical power button (tap on, hold off). Requires the hardware to be wired. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_FfbCurve0
data.value: Force curve point at 0% input (minimum force). E.g. raising it removes the dead zone at center.

data.name: SettingHelp_FfbCurve1
data.value: Force curve point at 25% input. E.g. brings out light road forces.

data.name: SettingHelp_FfbCurve2
data.value: Force curve point at 50% input. E.g. sets the middle of the response.

data.name: SettingHelp_FfbCurve3
data.value: Force curve point at 75% input. E.g. controls delivery in hard corners.

data.name: SettingHelp_FfbCurve4
data.value: Force curve point at 100% input (maximum force). E.g. lowering it compresses the peak without touching the rest.

data.name: SettingHelp_SpringGain
data.value: How much of the SPRING effect sent by the game is applied. E.g. 100% respects the game; 50% softens the return to center.

data.name: SettingHelp_DamperGain
data.value: How much of the DAMPER effect sent by the game is applied. E.g. lower it if the wheel feels too heavy when still.

data.name: SettingHelp_FrictionGain
data.value: How much of the FRICTION effect sent by the game is applied. E.g. lower it if steering feels dragged.

data.name: SettingHelp_InertiaGain
data.value: How much of the INERTIA effect sent by the game is applied. E.g. it simulates wheel mass when starting to turn.

data.name: SettingHelp_TorqueConstant
data.value: Motor torque constant (Nm per amp) — the exchange rate between requested force and current sent. With 0 the base uses the datasheet figure (0.55 Nm/A for the hoverboard motor) and the monitor shows a dash for estimated torque. Worth measuring: a wrong Kt raises no error, it just delivers less force than the screen claims. E.g. asking for 12 Nm at 0.55 sends 21.8 A; if the real Kt is 0.40, only 8.7 Nm reach the wheel. Takes effect on the next base restart.

data.name: SettingHelp_ThermalContinuousPct
data.value: Percentage of current considered safe continuously. E.g. 85% of peak. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_ThermalPeakSeconds
data.value: How many seconds peak current is tolerated before backing off. E.g. 10 s. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_FetTempLimitC
data.value: Temperature at which the board STARTS reducing force to protect itself; 20 degrees above that it cuts out completely. E.g. 85 degrees, the default — derating from 85, zero at 105. Only takes effect after the base reboots.

data.name: SettingHelp_MotorTempLimitC
data.value: Maximum motor temperature before disarming. E.g. 105 degrees. Requires the NTC sensor wired. [NOTE] This control has no effect in the current firmware yet.

data.name: SettingHelp_MotorEnable
data.value: Bring-up safety latch: the base starts DISARMED and only responds to commands with this on. E.g. after flashing for the first time, check board/encoder/motor in the fields below, enable here, and if anything goes wrong turn it off — the motor disarms immediately.

data.name: SettingHelp_CurrentLim
data.value: Maximum current the firmware lets reach the coils. It describes YOUR motor: higher than it can take means heat, lower means wasted torque. E.g. 25 A on the bench hoverboard motor. It also caps the calibration current.

data.name: Curve_Desc
data.value: How much force comes out for each force the game asks for. Drag the points. The dashed line is the reference: on it, what comes out equals what goes in. Below it in the middle means flattened mid-range forces — the wheel feels weak for most of the lap even with strong peaks.

data.name: Curve_Help
data.value:
Shapes how much force the base delivers for each force the game asks for.
HOW TO READ IT: the dashed line is the reference — on it, what comes out is exactly what the game asked for. Where your curve sits BELOW the dashed line, the base delivers less than asked; ABOVE, it delivers more.
WHERE YOU DRIVE: the middle of the graph (25% to 75%) is most of a lap — ordinary cornering, line corrections, the car sliding a little. The ends are the extremes: kerbs, impacts, a locked wheel. Changing the middle changes the whole lap; changing the end only changes the jolts.
WHAT IT IS FOR: raising the middle makes light forces more noticeable, and that is where grip information lives. Lowering the right end trims only the peaks without removing detail elsewhere — that is how you tame hard impacts without leaving the base soft.
THE TRAP: a curve that sags in the middle leaves the base WEAK for most of the lap and still clipping at the peaks. You compensate by raising the game's gain, and then only the jolts come through in full. If your curve sits well below the dashed line in the middle, that is what is happening.
Start from the straight line. Change little, one point at a time, and drive a lap between adjustments.
This curve applies AFTER linearity and BEFORE the torque and current limits — it shapes the force, it does not raise the base's ceiling.

data.name: FT_Desc
data.value: Each test applies one kind of force and concludes something about your base from what it answered. Run them top to bottom: they go from gentlest to strongest.

data.name: FT_Warning
data.value: ⚠️ This moves the wheel for real. Take your hands off the rim before starting, keep the Stop button in sight, and do not test with anyone next to the rig.

data.name: FT_StrengthHint
data.value: Scales the force each test asks for. Start low and raise gradually — a "100% peak" test with this at 10% applies 10%.

data.name: FT_NeedForce
data.value: The motor is not armed, so no test can run. If "Enable motor" is already on in the Hardware tab, it DISARMED — by protection or by a fault — and will not come back on its own: power-cycle the base. That switch is your permission to arm, not the motor's state.

data.name: ForceTest_Spring_Desc
data.value: Turn the wheel away from centre and run it. The base should pull it back. If it PUSHES away instead, the encoder direction is inverted — and this is the fastest way to find that without loading a game.

data.name: ForceTest_Vibration_Desc
data.value: Sweeps through frequencies at low force, looking for one that shakes the whole rig. This is how you find a loose mount or bolt — on track everything happens at once and you cannot separate them.

data.name: ForceTest_Ramp_Desc
data.value: Ramps force to maximum while watching the current follow. Answers whether the base delivers what the settings promise: the real ceiling is max current × Kt, and it can sit well below the number on screen.

data.name: ForceTest_Impact_Desc
data.value: Three short hits, alternating sides, like striking a kerb. Shows whether the peak comes out whole or the force path clips it.

data.name: SettingHelp_BrakeResistanceOhm
data.value: The resistance of the brake resistor YOU fitted — the value printed on it. The board does not measure it: it trusts this number to work out the current and power going through the resistor, and that is the figure that decides when to back off for heat. E.g. this bench uses a 2 ohm resistor; some builds use 12. Declaring 2 ohm with a 12 ohm resistor fitted gets that sum wrong by six times. Only takes effect after the base reboots.

data.name: SettingHelp_CurrentBandwidthHz
data.value: How fast the current loop chases the value asked for. The P and I gains are DERIVED from this and from the motor's R and L — there is nothing to tune by hand. E.g. 200 Hz on this bench; too high makes the motor whine and buzz, too low leaves the force soft and late. Only takes effect after the base reboots.

data.name: PB_Desc
data.value: Loads a lap someone recorded from a real game and plays the same forces on your wheel — no game needed. With the video of that same lap playing beside you, you see and feel the corner at the same time. It is also the only way to compare two settings on exactly the same lap.

data.name: PB_Warning
data.value: ⚠️ This is force with NO DRIVER IN THE LOOP. The lap was recorded with someone holding the wheel and reacting to every load; here there may be nobody. What was "cornering weight" against their hands becomes the wheel spinning on its own. Start at a low cap, take your hands off the rim, and keep Stop in sight.

data.name: PB_NoLap
data.value: No lap loaded. Recordings are .dlffb files — yours, or one someone shared.

data.name: PB_CapHint
data.value: How much of the recorded force actually comes out. Starts at 30% on purpose: you do not yet know what that lap does. Raise it once you have felt it.

data.name: PB_VideoHint
data.value: Open this video, pause it at the second the lap starts, and press Play at the same time you press the button below. The countdown gives you time for both.

data.name: PB_SyncHint
data.value: If what you feel arrives before or after what you see, nudge it here — you can do it while it plays. The error is constant, so getting it right once fixes the whole lap.

data.name: PB_NeedForce
data.value: The motor is not armed, so nothing can play. If "Enable motor" is already on in the Hardware tab, it DISARMED — by protection or by a fault — and will not come back on its own: power-cycle the base.

data.name: PB_Countdown
data.value: Take your hands off the rim — the force is about to start.
